title: Heated fin (convection)
sentence: A fin with assumed aluminium properties, held at its root temperature and cooled by air on all four long faces — steady conduction against the 1D fin formula.
theory: A fin of perimeter $P$ and area $A$ losing heat at $h$ into air at $T_\infty$ obeys $\dfrac{T(x) - T_\infty}{T_b - T_\infty} = \dfrac{\cosh m(L-x)}{\cosh mL}$ with $m = \sqrt{\dfrac{hP}{kA}}$, provided the cross-section is at one temperature. That holds when the Biot number $\mathrm{Bi} = \dfrac{h\,t/2}{k}$ is small — here $2.4\times10^{-4}$. With $m = 16.23\,\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and $L = 150\,\mathrm{mm}$ the tip sits at $37.39\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The numerical aluminium constants, including conductivity 205 W/(m K), are assumed reference inputs, not certified 6061-T6 or EN 573-3 material data.
